plan.title: docs(scope): document CompletionProvenance as a historical audit snapshot

narratives.Description: docs(scope): document CompletionProvenance as a historical audit snapshot
narratives.Overview:
> Recut after a single-critic arc refuted the framing. This was filed as a defect — fourteen fields written, one read. The inventory is accurate; the inference was wrong. A completion artifact is an audit record, and audit records do not need machine readers. What survives is documentation. Prior body and full critique record are in this issue's history and comments.

## Problem

`CompletionProvenance` (`packages/core/src/scope/delivery-evidence.ts:44-61`) declares thirteen required fields plus optional `completedSessionId`. Production code reads exactly one of them — `disposition`, via `classifyStoredDeliveryDisposition` — at three call sites that are a log suffix, a cohort log line, and a warning string.

**That is fine, and nothing in the source says so.** A reader running the same inventory reaches the same wrong conclusion, which is what happened here.

## Why write-only is correct

`main.md` states the standing of these artifacts directly:

> Completed xBRIEFs are evidence of what was built — **full standing as a record of *what is***, zero authority over *what to build next* (#3383).

The swarm lifecycle references call the post-merge lifecycle commit the authoritative record, and `content/docs/directive-lifecycle.md` distinguishes delivery, integration-only, explicit non-delivery, deployment and UAT as separate facts. #3041 deliberately required the repository, commit, PR, branch and verifier metadata, and made deploy and UAT explicit-only precisely because Git cannot infer them.

So a field needs a **reconstruction purpose**, not a present machine reader. Judging an audit record by current code readership is the same error as deleting logs because nothing greps them.

## Why removal would be actively harmful

Dropping repository, PR base, implementation or merge commits, verification time and actor, or explicit deploy and UAT facts creates a **permanent hole in every record written after the change**. Branches are deleted, refs move, forge APIs change. The moment those fields are wanted is a later incident analysis that has to reconstruct a completion decision from the artifact alone — exactly when re-deriving them is impossible.

## The economics argument is withdrawn

The original body claimed this affects #3631's and #3680's economics. Measured across eight recent one-artifact lifecycle commits, the provenance block is 15–16 lines and 541–629 bytes against artifacts of 138–377 lines — a median 6.9% of lines and 4.6% of bytes.

More decisively: **shrinking the JSON does not remove the lifecycle PR or its fixed CI cost.** That claim mistook variable payload size for the fixed cost of opening a PR and running its jobs. It has been withdrawn from #3631 and #3680.

## Fix

A short source comment on `CompletionProvenance` recording that it is a historical audit snapshot whose fields need not have current machine readers, grouping fields by the reconstruction question each answers — identity and location, delivery evidence, verification attribution, and explicit operator-supplied facts.

Note the `completedSessionId` duplication: the field is declared and stamped **nested inside** `completionProvenance`, while its consumer `packages/core/src/check/session-completed-ac.ts:159` reads the **sibling top-level** `plan.metadata.completedSessionId`. Two copies, one consumed. This is the block's one genuine redundancy question, and documenting which copy is authoritative is enough for now.

## Explicitly rejected

**Removing any field.** Refuted above.

**Adding machine readers so the inventory looks alive.** Artificial consumers optimize an inventory metric rather than an operator need.

**Duplicating #3679's work.** The `transition.ts` reader of stored disposition sits inside a branch guarded by `STATUS_PRECONDITIONS[act]`, which contains only `block` and `unblock`, so it cannot execute for `complete`. That dead path is real and #3679 owns making it reachable. This issue's only contribution is the finding that **what it prints is worth printing** — `DeliveryDisposition` distinguishes six outcomes, and "already completed" does not tell an operator which terminal claim is stored.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `CompletionProvenance` carries a comment stating it is a historical audit snapshot and that fields need not have current machine readers
- [ ] Fields are grouped by the reconstruction question each answers
- [ ] The `completedSessionId` duplication is documented, naming which copy consumers read
- [ ] No field is removed
- [ ] No synthetic reader is added
- [ ] No change to `transition.ts`, `STATUS_PRECONDITIONS`, or the dead branch — that is #3679
- [ ] CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]` line

## Critique record

Triage write-back [5400552126](https://github.com/deftai/directive/issues/3690#issuecomment-5400552126) · Stop 2 N=1 · critic [5400636108](https://github.com/deftai/directive/issues/3690#issuecomment-5400636108) · successor lean below.

Related: #3679 (owns the dead branch), #3041 (designed these fields), #3631 and #3680 (economics claim withdrawn from both). Closed as refuted in the same family: #3686, #3689.


---

## Issue comment thread

_The issue body is the original write-up; maintainer comments below may supersede it. Read the full thread before building a dispatch envelope (#2143)._

### Comment by @MScottAdams (2026-08-24T19:55:34Z)

model: claude-opus-5
role: triage

mechanism-shaped: true

design-critique: warranted, because the issue treats a write-only record as a defect without establishing that audit records are supposed to be read by code, and because two designs in this same family were already refuted today for reasoning that felt equally obvious.

## Disclosure

I filed this today. It came out of the #3686 panel, where a critic inventoried `completionProvenance` consumers and found almost none; I reproduced that inventory before filing.

**My conflict is specific and worth naming.** This is the last surviving issue from a line of work that consumed most of today. #3686 proposed moving delivery provenance to a post-merge receipt and was refuted by its own panel. #3689 proposed batching lifecycle lands and was refuted by its own panel. Both are closed. #3680 was parked on a premise that turned out void, then unparked and rescoped after I measured that its central claim was drawn from a biased sample.

If #3690 also collapses, the family produced one landed CI change and a stack of closed issues. **I have an incentive for this one to be real.** A critic should test the framing rather than the inventory — the inventory is measured and will hold; whether it means anything is the question.

I have also been wrong twice today in the same direction: treating a refutation as a positive result, and generalizing from a biased sample. Both times the error was moving too fast from "X is not true" to "therefore Y."

## Confidence

**Measured, and re-verified at `90e59d41` just now:**

`CompletionProvenance` declares fourteen fields — thirteen required plus optional `completedSessionId` (`packages/core/src/scope/delivery-evidence.ts`).

Production reads only `disposition`, via `classifyStoredDeliveryDisposition`. Its three call sites are a log suffix in `transition.ts`, a log line in `swarm/complete-cohort.ts`, and warning text in `swarm/finalize-cohort.ts`. No gate, report, doctor check or `task check` surface reads `mergeCommit`, `verifiedAt`, `verifier`, or the other stored fields back from an artifact.

`STATUS_PRECONDITIONS` still contains only `block` and `unblock`, so the `transition.ts` reader — written under #3041 for `act === "complete" && currentFolder === "completed"` — remains unreachable. One of three consumers is dead code.

`delivery-evidence.ts` reads `evidence.mergeCommit` at gate time, but that is the gate's *input*, not a read of a stored record.

**Asserted, and this is where the issue is weak:**

That write-only-ness is a defect. I did not establish that a completion artifact is supposed to have code readers. An audit record whose only consumer is a human reading history later is not obviously broken.

That the fields cost enough to be worth reconsidering. I asserted this affects #3631's and #3680's economics without measuring how much of a lifecycle diff or review surface fourteen fields actually represent.

That `deployed` and `uatVerified` being explicitly operator-supplied (#3041) makes them different in kind. I said so in the body but did not follow it to its conclusion — if two fields are deliberately for humans, others may be too, and "no code reader" stops being diagnostic.

```
audit:fourteen-fields sha=90e59d41 pointer=packages/core/src/scope/delivery-evidence.ts:44-60 reading=measured
audit:one-field-read sha=90e59d41 pointer=packages/core/src/scope/delivery-evidence.ts:188-201 reading=measured
audit:dead-reader sha=90e59d41 pointer=packages/core/src/scope/constants.ts:45-48 reading=measured
audit:writeonly-is-defect sha=90e59d41 pointer=comment:none reading=asserted
audit:payload-costs-enough sha=90e59d41 pointer=comment:none reading=asserted
```

## Refutation target

> **A field with no production code consumer is a defect worth removing or justifying, rather than the normal shape of an audit record.**

This is the framing the whole issue rests on and it is the part I did not test.

The opposing position, which deserves a real hearing: delivery provenance is an *audit* record. Audit records are written so that a human — or a future tool nobody has built — can reconstruct what happened. Judging them by current code readership is the same category error as deleting logs because nothing greps them. On that reading the inventory is accurate and the conclusion inverted, and the correct output is documentation of who each field is for, not a smaller payload.

If that holds, this issue shrinks to a comment block and the family's last live thread closes with it.

## Notes for the critic

**Do not spend effort re-verifying the inventory.** It is measured, I reproduced it independently of the critic who found it, and it will hold. Spend the pass on whether it means what the issue says it means.

**The dead reader is a separate fact and survives either way.** Code written under #3041 for a specific recovery case has never executed. #3679 owns making it reachable; this issue owns whether what it prints is worth printing. That is true whether or not the framing survives.

**Consider who else might read this.** Look for consumers outside `packages/` — docs, skills, packs, templates, or human-facing process that instructs someone to read a completed artifact. If the framework tells operators to inspect provenance, "no code reader" is answering the wrong question. I only searched `packages/core/src` and `packages/cli/src`.

**Two prior issues in this family were refuted for reasoning that felt as solid as this does.** If the framing is wrong, say so plainly — closing this cleanly is a better outcome than shipping a payload change nobody needed.

role: parent

## Stop 2 - variant selection

**Charter:** refutation. Target from the triage write-back: *a field with no production code consumer is a defect worth removing or justifying, rather than the normal shape of an audit record.*

**Spend:** N=1. Input ceiling is the triage write-back, comment `5400552126`.

**Why not a panel.** The inventory is already measured and reproduced twice, so critics would not be decorrelating over the facts. What is untested is a single framing question with an enumerable answer set - audit records are write-mostly by design, or they are not - and one critic reading primary sources settles it. Blast radius is bounded: the worst case is a documentation change to one interface.

Tenth arc today. Panels have been spent where being wrong was expensive and hard to reverse; this is neither.

**Standing risk recorded.** Two issues in this family were refuted by their own panels today, and the parent has a disclosed interest in this one surviving. The critic is explicitly invited to close the framing rather than improve it.


### Comment by @MScottAdams (2026-08-24T20:01:55Z)

model: gpt-5.6-sol
role: critic

SHA: `90e59d41267fb922ec97d676139a217915e575dc`

Input ceiling honored: issue #3690 body plus comments with id `<= 5400552126` only. The sole in-envelope comment is the triage write-back `5400552126`.

## Steelman

The strongest case for the issue is not “unused fields are always dead.” It is that a mandatory record has a recurring review and schema cost, null-valued fields can create false confidence, and speculative fields can become permanent compatibility baggage. The block also duplicates `completedSessionId` at `plan.metadata.completedSessionId` and inside `completionProvenance`, while the production check reads the top-level value. I would flip toward field removal if a field could not be tied to a reconstruction question, if operators were demonstrably misreading it, or if measured lifecycle cost was material.

That evidence is absent. The current evidence points the other way.

## Audit-marker dispositions

| Marker | Disposition | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| `audit:fourteen-fields` (measured) | **verified** | `CompletionProvenance` has thirteen required fields plus optional `completedSessionId` at this SHA ([source](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/90e59d41267fb922ec97d676139a217915e575dc/packages/core/src/scope/delivery-evidence.ts#L44-L61)). |
| `audit:one-field-read` (measured) | **verified under the stated stored-record method** | Stored `completionProvenance` is read for `disposition`; its three production call sites are operator text. The `verify:ac` reader reads the sibling top-level `plan.metadata.completedSessionId`, not the nested copy, so it does not falsify this marker ([classifier](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/90e59d41267fb922ec97d676139a217915e575dc/packages/core/src/scope/delivery-evidence.ts#L184-L207)). |
| `audit:dead-reader` (measured) | **verified** | `STATUS_PRECONDITIONS` contains only `block` and `unblock`, so the `complete`-specific branch under `requiredStatus !== undefined` cannot execute ([preconditions](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/90e59d41267fb922ec97d676139a217915e575dc/packages/core/src/scope/constants.ts#L44-L48), [dead branch](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/90e59d41267fb922ec97d676139a217915e575dc/packages/core/src/scope/transition.ts#L175-L187)). |
| `audit:writeonly-is-defect` (asserted) | **refuted** | Directive explicitly gives completed xBRIEFs “full standing as a record of what is” and calls the post-merge lifecycle commit the authoritative record ([main](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/90e59d41267fb922ec97d676139a217915e575dc/main.md#L193-L208), [swarm lifecycle record](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/90e59d41267fb922ec97d676139a217915e575dc/content/skills/deft-directive-swarm/references/core-phase-5-6.md#L284-L298)). #3041 deliberately required repository/commit/PR/branch/verifier metadata and separate deployment/UAT axes. Current code readership is therefore the wrong sufficiency test. |
| `audit:payload-costs-enough` (asserted) | **not substantiated; withdraw** | In eight recent one-artifact lifecycle commits (`90e59d41`, `4646bd7f`, `bf3929c1`, `e33b1d6c`, `8bb1e528`, `3d3e9ca9`, `09ef0fde`, `b37c5aac`), the block is 15–16 lines and 541–629 bytes. The artifacts are 138–377 lines; median block share is 6.9% of lines and 4.6% of bytes. Removing it does not remove the lifecycle PR or its fixed CI cost. No review-time or storage-cost evidence was supplied. |

## Findings

### blocks-the-design — Code readership is a category error for this record

**Evidence.** The framework says completed xBRIEFs are evidence of what was built and the authoritative cross-session/post-swarm lifecycle record. The lifecycle documentation distinguishes delivery, integration-only, explicit non-delivery, deployment, and UAT facts ([lifecycle semantics](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/90e59d41267fb922ec97d676139a217915e575dc/content/docs/directive-lifecycle.md#L68-L90)). #3041’s acceptance criteria expressly required the reconstruction fields now being questioned ([#3041](https://github.com/deftai/directive/issues/3041)).

**Failure mode.** Dropping repository, PR/base, implementation/merge/delivery commits, verification time/actor, or explicit deploy/UAT facts creates a permanent hole in records written after the change. Branches can be deleted, refs can move, APIs can disappear, and later incident analysis cannot reconstruct the completion decision from the artifact itself. Under the shared-state/swarm lens, this record is a durable handoff between workers, operators, clones, and future sessions; deletion saves hundreds of bytes by weakening that handoff.

**Disposition consequence.** The proposed payload-reduction design cannot bind. The refutation target is refuted.

### sharpens-framing — The surviving work is documentation, not deletion

**Evidence.** Field purpose is recoverable, but spread across #3041, `directive-lifecycle.md`, interface comments, and lifecycle skills. The source does not locally say that `CompletionProvenance` is a historical audit snapshot whose fields need not have current machine readers.

**Failure mode.** A later inventory can repeat the same “no reader means dead” inference, while a broad keep-everything reaction can also shelter genuinely redundant fields. `completedSessionId` is the concrete edge case: the nested copy is not the value consumed by `verify:ac`; the top-level sibling is.

**Disposition consequence.** Reduce this issue to a short comment block that groups the fields by reconstruction role and explains the nested session correlation. Do not add synthetic readers merely to make the inventory look alive.

### sharpens-framing — The payload-economics argument does not survive measurement

**Evidence.** The eight-commit sample above measures the actual serialized block against actual artifact-only lifecycle diffs at the target SHA: median 16 lines / 611 bytes, 6.9% of added artifact lines and 4.6% of artifact bytes.

**Failure mode.** Calling this a substantial driver of lifecycle-PR economics mistakes variable payload size for the fixed cost of opening a lifecycle PR and running its jobs. Shrinking the JSON leaves that fixed cost intact.

**Disposition consequence.** Withdraw the economics claim from #3631/#3680 reasoning unless a measured review-time, storage, or CI relationship is produced.

### sharpens-framing — The dead disposition reader is real and worth reviving under #3679

**Evidence.** The branch is unreachable as measured. `DeliveryDisposition` distinguishes `delivered`, `merged_to_integration`, `not_delivered`, explicit non-delivery outcomes, `unknown`, and `unverified`; “already completed” is not enough to tell an operator which terminal claim is stored.

**Failure mode.** A recovery/re-complete attempt suppresses the distinction #3041 introduced, so an operator cannot tell from the command response whether the artifact claims delivery or an accepted non-delivery terminal state.

**Disposition consequence.** #3679 should make the path reachable/restampable. What it prints is worth printing. This does not justify shrinking `completionProvenance`, and #3690 should not duplicate #3679’s recovery implementation.

### footnote — `completedSessionId` is duplicated, not consumed from the nested block

The nested field is stamped for a self-contained provenance snapshot, while `session-completed-ac.ts` reads `plan.metadata.completedSessionId`. This is a precise candidate for documentation or later normalization, but its roughly one-line cost does not change this issue’s disposition.

## Road not taken

I rejected adding code consumers for every field. Artificial readers would optimize for an inventory metric rather than an operator need. I also rejected deleting every currently unread field: most fields answer durable reconstruction questions that cannot be safely recovered later. The proportionate path is to document the audit contract now and add machine readers only when a real decision surface needs them.

## Verdict

**Refutation target: refuted.**

**Recommendation: reduce to documentation.** Replace the bug-shaped payload review with a short source comment that states this is a historical audit snapshot and groups who each field serves; withdraw the economics claim. Leave the reachable/restampable disposition behavior to #3679.

Plain answer: a write-only audit record is **the expected shape here**, not a defect. A field still needs a reconstruction purpose, but it does not need a present production-code reader.


### Comment by @MScottAdams (2026-08-24T20:03:01Z)

model: claude-opus-5
role: parent

Successor lean. Round 1 was a single critic against ceiling `5400552126`. All five findings accepted.

## The framing is refuted by the framework's own constitution

I asked the critic to test whether write-only-ness is a defect rather than the expected shape of an audit record. It is the expected shape, and `main.md` says so directly:

> Completed xBRIEFs are evidence of what was built — **full standing as a record of *what is***, zero authority over *what to build next* (#3383).

The swarm lifecycle references call the post-merge lifecycle commit the authoritative record, and #3041 deliberately required the repository, commit, PR, branch and verifier metadata this issue questioned — along with deployment and UAT as separate explicit axes precisely because they cannot be inferred.

So current code readership is the wrong sufficiency test. `audit:writeonly-is-defect` is **refuted**. A field needs a reconstruction purpose; it does not need a present machine reader.

The failure mode the critic named is the one that matters: dropping repository, PR base, implementation or merge commits, verification time and actor, or explicit deploy and UAT facts creates a **permanent hole in every record written after the change**. Branches get deleted, refs move, APIs disappear. A later incident analysis has to reconstruct the completion decision from the artifact itself, and that is exactly when the fields would be wanted.

## My economics claim does not survive measurement

`audit:payload-costs-enough` is **withdrawn**. Across eight recent one-artifact lifecycle commits the provenance block is 15–16 lines and 541–629 bytes, against artifacts of 138–377 lines — a median 6.9% of lines and 4.6% of bytes.

And the deeper error: shrinking the JSON does not remove the lifecycle PR or its fixed CI cost. I mistook variable payload size for the fixed cost of opening a PR and running its jobs. That claim is being withdrawn from #3631's and #3680's bodies, where I planted it today.

## What the critic found that I missed

`completedSessionId` is **duplicated**. It is declared nested inside `CompletionProvenance` and stamped there, while the actual consumer — `session-completed-ac.ts:159` — reads the sibling top-level `plan.metadata.completedSessionId`. I verified both. That is a precise documentation or normalization candidate, and it is the one field in the block with a genuine redundancy question rather than an imagined one.

## What survives

The three measured markers are verified. The inventory was accurate; only the inference was wrong.

**The dead reader stands and is worth reviving.** `STATUS_PRECONDITIONS` holds only `block` and `unblock`, so the `complete`-specific branch cannot execute. The critic's argument for why it matters is better than mine: `DeliveryDisposition` distinguishes `delivered`, `merged_to_integration`, `not_delivered`, explicit non-delivery outcomes, `unknown` and `unverified`, and "already completed" does not tell an operator which terminal claim is stored. #3679 owns making the path reachable. What it prints is worth printing.

## Decisions

**Reduce to documentation.** Replace the payload review with a short source comment on `CompletionProvenance` stating that it is a historical audit snapshot whose fields need not have current machine readers, grouped by the reconstruction question each field answers. Note the `completedSessionId` duplication and which copy is consumed.

**Do not remove any field.** Refuted.

**Do not add synthetic readers.** The critic's road-not-taken is right — artificial consumers would optimize an inventory metric rather than an operator need.

**Withdraw the economics claim** from #3631 and #3680.

**Leave the dead branch to #3679.** This issue does not duplicate that recovery work.

## A pattern worth naming

This is the third issue I filed in this family today and the third refuted by its own critic. #3686 proposed a post-merge receipt. #3689 proposed batching lands. #3690 proposed shrinking a payload.

All three shared one error. Each began with a correct measurement — the ancestry gate does force a second write, lifecycle PRs are 46 of 54 single-artifact, fourteen fields are written and one is read — and then inferred a fix the measurement did not support. The measurements all held under scrutiny. Every inference failed.

That is not three unlucky guesses; it is one habit. Recording it here rather than only in the closing note, because the next person reading this family should see it.

```
audit:record-standing sha=90e59d41 pointer=main.md:201 reading=measured
audit:session-id-duplicated sha=90e59d41 pointer=packages/core/src/check/session-completed-ac.ts:159 reading=measured
```

Both reproduced by the parent before adoption.
